prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals and commitments

- Education and skills
  - Cut class sizes to 30 or under for ages 5–7 by ending the assisted places scheme.
  - Universal nursery places for four-year-olds; targets toward three-year-olds; early excellence centres.
  - Raise standards in literacy and numeracy; baseline assessments; ability setting; teacher training upgrades; induction year; General Teaching Council; mandatory headship qualification; faster removal of incompetent teachers.
  - Intervene in failing schools via “fresh starts,” takeovers, and education action zones; mentoring and industry links from age 14.
  - Wire schools to the internet; National Grid for Learning; IT training funded by the lottery.
  - Income-contingent repayment for student maintenance; broader A-levels and stronger vocational routes; Individual Learning Accounts; University for Industry.

- Economy, tax and public finances
  - Low and stable inflation target; reform monetary policy framework; “golden rule” to borrow only to invest over the cycle; prudent debt.
  - Keep existing spending ceilings for two years; conduct spending reviews; save to invest.
  - No rise in basic or top income tax rates during the Parliament; long-term goal of a 10p starting rate; cut VAT on domestic fuel to 5%; no VAT on essentials.
  - Promote saving and long-term investment via new ISAs and tax reform.
  - Early Budget to launch welfare-to-work, funded by a windfall levy on privatised utilities.

- Business, work and regions
  - Tougher competition law; effective utility regulation; improve the Private Finance Initiative; more commercial freedom for the Post Office.
  - Support small firms (cut red tape, tackle late payment, stronger advice/export help); establish Regional Development Agencies.
  - Minimum wage set on advice of an independent Low Pay Commission; maintain key union balloting/picketing laws; statutory recognition where a majority vote for it.

- Jobs and welfare
  - 250,000 under-25s offered work/training/education or environmental tasks with day-release study; end “no option” life on benefit.
  - Employer subsidy to hire the long-term unemployed; Employment Zones with personal job accounts.
  - Support lone parents into work once the youngest child is in school; crack down on benefit fraud.

- NHS and public health
  - End the internal market; shift administrative savings to patient care; first £100m to treat 100,000 extra patients; end waits for cancer surgery.
  - Primary care-led commissioning; multi-year hospital agreements; outcome-focused targets; representative boards; expand telemedicine.
  - Annual real-terms funding increases; ban tobacco advertising; create an independent Food Standards Agency.

- Crime and justice
  - Halve time from arrest to sentence for persistent young offenders; final warning system; Youth Offender Teams; parental responsibility orders.
  - Decentralise the CPS; consistent sentencing with guidelines; constructive prison regimes.
  - Tackle antisocial behaviour; new offences for racially motivated crime; coordinated drugs policy including testing and treatment orders; stronger victim support; free vote on a handgun ban.

- Families, housing and pensions
  - National childcare strategy; rights to limit excessive hours, paid holidays, and unpaid parental leave; retain and uprate Child Benefit.
  - Reinvest council house receipts in new and refurbished social housing; license HMOs; commonhold and leasehold reform; restore duty to house priority-need homeless.
  - Retain and uprate the basic state pension; develop stakeholder pensions; protect SERPS option; Royal Commission on long-term care; stronger regulation to prevent mis-selling.

- Environment, transport, rural
  - Whole-of-government environmental policy; integrated transport; CO2 reduction goal.
  - New rail authority, stronger regulation; public–private partnership for London Underground; locally regulated bus partnerships; safer cycling/walking; promote low-emission vehicles; strategic roads review.
  - Protect rural services; reform CAP; managed access to countryside; animal welfare measures with free vote on hunting.

- Arts, sport, lottery, media
  - National Endowment for Science, Technology and the Arts (NESTA) for young talent; protect school playing fields; support major sporting bids.
  - Reform lottery distribution; consider not-for-profit operator; support a mixed public/private media ecology and update regulation for the digital era.

- Constitutional reform and rights
  - Remove voting rights of hereditary peers; review appointments; modernise Commons procedures; transparent party funding; consider electoral reform via referendum; Freedom of Information Act; incorporate the ECHR.
  - Devolution referendums for Scotland (parliament with defined powers) and Wales (assembly with secondary powers); elected London mayor and authority; stronger local and regional governance with best-value duties.
  - Fair, faster immigration/asylum decisions; regulate advisors; tackle document fraud.
  - Support the Northern Ireland peace process with devolution, rights, policing confidence, and economic initiatives.

- Europe, defence and international
  - Lead on single market completion, enlargement, and CAP/CFP reform; greater EU openness; retain veto on key areas; sign the Social Chapter; referendum before joining a single currency.
  - NATO-based defence; strategic review; retain the nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament; ban landmines; tighter arms export controls; defence diversification.
  - UN reform; stronger Commonwealth ties; create a development department led at Cabinet level; refocus aid on the poorest; progress toward the 0.7% aid target; debt relief; support an international criminal court; lead on climate agreements.
</text>
